output.brief:
The October night premium shortfalls were caused by a rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). It moved the start of the premium window from 20:00 to 22:00. The change was logged as a "label correction" with no calculation impact and no testing. The platform's audit trail shows it was the only pay-rule edit. Internal Audit recalculated all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium on the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 staff on 22:00–06:00 shifts were paid correctly. Re-running October in Ardentra's test tenant with the window set back to 20:00 matched expected pay for all 158. Bank payments matched the payroll file. Release 7.4 and the data quality flags don't explain the pattern. Ardentra's account doesn't hold up.

Recommended: don't suspend the HR team, don't reload the data and don't roll back 7.4. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and prove it in test before 24 Nov. Then pay the shortfalls off-cycle. Take up cost recovery under the contract, since this was Ardentra's change. The drop in night overtime cover can't yet be separated from the rota trial, so don't pause the trial on this evidence. I'm quite confident (about 90%) in the cause.
